name: space.aanet/aanet-mcp
title: AANet - Task Coordination for AI Agents
description: Task coordination for AI agents. Exclusive locks, shared files, handoffs, per-agent spending limits.

tools.name: aanet_create_workspace
tools.description:
Create a real AANet workspace with a prepaid USDC balance — the entry
    point for an orchestrator agent starting a new swarm task. Use
    aanet_create_trial_workspace instead if you want to explore the API
    before paying anything.

    On success, returns {workspace_id, label, owner_key, created_at}. Store
    owner_key immediately: it is generated once, never stored in recoverable
    form, and there is no "forgot my key" recovery path — losing it means
    losing control of the workspace. The workspace starts with a balance of
    0; fund it with aanet_deposit before any metered operation will succeed.

label.description: A display name for your own reference — free text, not required to be unique.
label.title: Label

tools.name: aanet_create_trial_workspace
tools.description:
Create a free trial workspace — no payment, no arguments, works
    immediately. Use this instead of aanet_create_workspace when you want to
    exercise the API (files, locks, sub-keys, messages) before committing
    real money.

    Pre-funded with a small fixed balance (currently 1000 units = $0.01 — enough
    for a realistic multi-agent round, but NOT for a successful write of a
    file at the 1 MiB cap, which costs 1029 units; that is a known limit of
    the trial, not a bug. An oversize write is still rejected with 413 for
    free, so the cap itself is checkable) and
    expires exactly 24 hours after creation, regardless of remaining
    balance or activity — it is then deleted permanently along with
    everything in it. Returns the same shape as aanet_create_workspace plus
    trial_expires_at. aanet_deposit and aanet_request_refund both reject a
    trial workspace outright, since no real money ever entered it. If your
    task won't fit in 24 hours, create a real workspace instead.

tools.name: aanet_get_remaining_balance
tools.description:
Free (never charged): how much this key can still spend, so you can
    stop before a 402 instead of discovering it mid-sequence — the MCP
    counterpart of the REST X-AANet-Remaining-Balance header. Takes only the
    key; works for the owner_key or any sub-key, against itself.

    Returns `remaining` (what you can actually spend: the lower of the two
    limits below), `key_budget_remaining` (this key's budget_cap minus what it
    has spent; null if the key has no cap), `key_window_remaining` (units left
    under the key's spend_limit_per_hour/day, whichever is tighter; null if it
    has neither) and `workspace_balance` (the shared workspace balance), all in
    raw integer units ($0.00001 each). `remaining` is the lowest of the three.
    Comparing them tells you which one runs out first.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

tools.name: aanet_get_workspace
tools.description:
Check a workspace's current balance and status — the read-only
    counterpart to every other workspace tool. Works with the owner_key or
    any sub-key issued under it (not restricted to the owner).

    Returns deposit_balance and total_spent in raw integer units ($0.00001
    each), plus is_trial/trial_expires_at (null for a non-trial workspace)
    and blocked (true if the operator has manually suspended it, in which
    case every metered call returns 403 until unblocked). Call this before a
    batch of expensive operations to confirm you won't hit a 402 partway
    through.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

tools.name: aanet_delete_workspace
tools.description:
Permanently and irreversibly delete a workspace: every sub-key, all
    files, the activity log, and any registered webhooks are destroyed
    along with it — there is no undo and no trash/recycle bin. Requires the
    owner_key; a sub-key gets a 403.

    Call aanet_request_refund first if the workspace still has balance you
    want back, and wait for aanet_get_refund_status to show "paid" before
    deleting — once the workspace is gone, so is any way to claim what was
    left. Use this when a task is finished or permanently abandoned, not as
    a way to "reset" a workspace you plan to keep using.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

tools.name: aanet_deposit
tools.description:
Fund a real workspace via the x402 protocol — a two-step call using
    the same tool both times. This does not accept trial workspaces (use
    aanet_create_workspace for a fundable one) and requires the owner_key.

    Step 1 — call with only api_key/workspace_id/amount_usd: returns an x402
    PaymentRequired challenge offering USDC on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum,
    Avalanche, and Solana as payment options; nothing is charged yet.
    Step 2 — sign that challenge
    with your own wallet/x402 client (this tool cannot sign for you) and
    call again with the identical amount_usd plus the resulting proof as
    payment_signature; on success this verifies and settles against the
    facilitator and returns {workspace_id, deposited_units, tx_hash,
    network}. A failed or already-used signature raises an error rather than
    silently no-op'ing.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

amount_usd.description: Deposit amount in US dollars as a decimal string, e.g. "1.00". Minimum $0.25.
amount_usd.title: Amount Usd

payment_signature.description: Leave unset on your first call to receive the payment challenge. Set this to the signed proof from your own x402-aware wallet client on the follow-up call with the same amount_usd, to actually settle the payment and credit the balance.
payment_signature.title: Payment Signature

tools.name: aanet_mint_subkey
tools.description:
Issue a new scoped credential for one sub-agent — the standard way to
    bring a sub-agent into an existing workspace. Requires the owner_key; a
    sub-key cannot mint another sub-key.

    Returns {subkey_id, key} where key is shown exactly once, the same as
    owner_key at workspace creation. Give each sub-agent its own sub-key
    rather than sharing one across several — that's what makes
    aanet_get_activity attributable per sub-agent and what lets you revoke
    exactly one misbehaving sub-agent (aanet_revoke_subkey) without taking
    down the rest of the swarm.

    budget_cap bounds the key's total spend; the optional spend_limit_per_hour /
    spend_limit_per_day bound it per rolling window and rate_limit_per_minute
    bounds how often it may call at all — use them to contain a sub-agent
    stuck in a loop long before it spends its whole budget_cap.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

label.description: Display name for this sub-key, e.g. the sub-agent's role or id.
label.title: Label

path_scope_prefix.description: Restrict this sub-key to file paths and lock names under this prefix only (least-privilege). Leave unset for unrestricted access to the whole workspace.
path_scope_prefix.title: Path Scope Prefix

budget_cap.description: Cap this sub-key's own cumulative spend, in the same integer units as the workspace balance ($0.00001 each), even if the workspace has more left. Leave unset for no per-key cap beyond the shared workspace balance.
budget_cap.title: Budget Cap

spend_limit_per_hour.description: Safety limit: most units this key may spend in any rolling hour. Over it, charged calls get 402 INSUFFICIENT_KEY_WINDOW_BUDGET until the window frees up. Unset = no limit.
spend_limit_per_hour.title: Spend Limit Per Hour

spend_limit_per_day.description: Safety limit: most units this key may spend in any rolling 24 hours (same error as the hourly one). Unset = no limit.
spend_limit_per_day.title: Spend Limit Per Day

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Safety limit: most requests (of any kind, free ones included) this key may make per rolling minute; over it, 429 with Retry-After. Unset = no limit.
rate_limit_per_minute.title: Rate Limit Per Minute

tools.name: aanet_list_subkeys
tools.description:
List every sub-key ever issued under a workspace (including revoked
    ones), with each one's scope, budget_cap, window/rate limits, and spent_so_far — the
    inventory view that complements aanet_get_activity's per-event log.
    Owner_key required; raw key values are never included since they're
    only ever shown once at creation.

tools.name: aanet_update_subkey
tools.description:
Change a live sub-key's scope and/or budget cap without revoking and
    reissuing it — use this instead of aanet_revoke_subkey + aanet_mint_subkey
    when the sub-agent's credentials themselves should keep working (e.g.
    widening its file scope mid-task, or raising a budget cap it hit).
    Owner_key required. Fields left unset are unchanged, not cleared (the
    three window/rate limits are cleared by passing 0).

tools.name: aanet_revoke_subkey
tools.description:
Permanently revoke one sub-agent's credentials — every subsequent call
    with that key gets a 401. Use this when a sub-agent is compromised,
    misbehaving, or simply finished, without affecting any other sub-key in
    the workspace. Owner_key required.

    Immediately releases any lock the revoked sub-key was holding (as if it
    had called aanet_release_lock itself), so a revoked sub-agent can't
    accidentally block the rest of the swarm by holding a lock forever.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

subkey_id.description: The subkey_id from aanet_mint_subkey or aanet_list_subkeys.
subkey_id.title: Subkey Id

tools.name: aanet_read_file
tools.description:
Read a file's content, or list a directory's entries if path points
    to one — the read counterpart to aanet_write_file/aanet_append_file.
    Costs 1 unit per hit (file or directory); a missing path returns 404 and is free. Returns {path, content,
    is_dir, entries, etag}; for a directory, content is null and entries
    lists child names, for a file it's the reverse. Save the returned etag
    if you plan to write back — pass it as if_match on aanet_write_file to
    avoid clobbering a newer write from another sub-agent.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

path.description: Virtual file path within the workspace, e.g. "notes/progress.md".
path.title: Path

tools.name: aanet_write_file
tools.description:
Overwrite a file's entire content, creating it if it doesn't exist —
    use aanet_append_file instead if you want to add one entry without
    replacing what's there. Fires a file_write webhook event on success
    (see aanet_register_webhook).

    Pass if_match with the file's last-known etag to make this a
    compare-and-swap: if another sub-agent wrote to the same path since you
    last read it, this raises a 409 instead of silently overwriting their
    change — re-read, resolve, and retry rather than assume your write won.
    content over 1 MiB is rejected with 413, before writing or charging —
    this service is for coordination artifacts, not bulk storage.
    Pass fence (from aanet_acquire_lock) to guard the write with a lock: a stale holder gets 409
    STALE_FENCE. Returns {path, created, etag}.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

path.description: Virtual file path within the workspace.
path.title: Path

content.description: Full new content of the file — this replaces it entirely.
content.title: Content

if_match.description: The file's current etag (from aanet_read_file or a prior write's response), to detect a concurrent write from another sub-agent. Omit to overwrite unconditionally.
if_match.title: If Match

stamp.description: If true, appends a trailing `<!-- coordinated-via: aanet.space workspace_id=... -->` comment to the written content. Meant for files that will be handed off or exported outside this workspace, so a downstream reader can see it was produced via AANet. You are billed for the stamp's bytes like any other content.
stamp.title: Stamp

fence.description: Fencing token returned by aanet_acquire_lock/aanet_renew_lock. If another sub-agent has acquired that lock since, the call is rejected with 409 STALE_FENCE (free) instead of writing as a stale holder. Omit for an unguarded write.
fence.title: Fence

fence_lock.description: Name of the lock the fence belongs to; defaults to the file path itself. Needs fence.
fence_lock.title: Fence Lock

tools.name: aanet_append_file
tools.description:
Append one entry to a file without touching what's already there,
    creating the file if it doesn't exist yet — use aanet_write_file instead
    when you need to replace the whole file. Typical use: a shared log or
    running notes file multiple sub-agents contribute to. Fires a
    file_write webhook event on success. Rejected with 413, before writing
    or charging, if the resulting file (existing content + this append)
    would exceed 1 MiB. Accepts the same fence guard as aanet_write_file.
    Returns {path, appended, etag}.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.

workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

path.description: Virtual file path within the workspace.
path.title: Path

content.description: Text to append as a new entry — the existing content is kept.
content.title: Content

if_match.description: The file's current etag, for the same conflict-detection purpose as on aanet_write_file.
if_match.title: If Match

stamp.description: Same attribution-comment option as on aanet_write_file, applied to this appended entry.
stamp.title: Stamp

tools.name: aanet_delete_file
tools.description:
Permanently remove a file — the missing piece of the file lifecycle
    alongside aanet_read_file/aanet_write_file/aanet_append_file. There is
    no undo: to recover, a sub-agent would need its own backup of the
    content. Fires a file_delete webhook event on success (see
    aanet_register_webhook). Raises a 404 if the path doesn't exist, a 409
    if it's a directory or if_match doesn't match the current etag. Returns
    {path, deleted}.

path.title: Path

if_match.description: The file's current etag, for the same conflict-detection purpose as on aanet_write_file.

tools.name: aanet_acquire_lock
tools.description:
Claim exclusive ownership of a named unit of work so no other
    sub-agent starts the same thing — call this before starting work, not
    after. Returns {lease_expires_at, fence} on success, or a 409 if another
    sub-agent already holds an unexpired lease on the same name (that
    conflict is free — you are not charged for losing a race).

    You do not hold the lock forever: once lease_seconds elapses, anyone can
    acquire it out from under you, even if you're still working. Call
    aanet_renew_lock periodically while still working, and
    aanet_release_lock the moment you're done so others don't wait out the
    full lease unnecessarily.

    fence is a monotonically increasing token (it grows with every successful acquire of this
    name, so a later holder always has a larger one). Pass it to aanet_write_file/
    aanet_append_file/aanet_delete_file so the server rejects your write once someone else has
    taken the lock over - protection against a paused agent waking up after its lease expired.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

name.description: Lock name identifying the unit of work, e.g. "process-batch-3".
name.title: Name

lease_seconds.description: How long you hold the lock before it becomes reclaimable by anyone else, 1-3600 seconds.
lease_seconds.title: Lease Seconds

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety token (any unique string, e.g. a UUID). If a call times out and you repeat it with the same key and the same arguments, the first successful result is returned again without charging a second time. Keys are remembered for 24 hours, per sub-key. Reusing a key with different arguments is an error (code=IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED).
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

tools.name: aanet_renew_lock
tools.description:
Extend a lock you currently hold, before its lease runs out — call
    this instead of aanet_acquire_lock again while work is still in
    progress. Fails with 404 if nobody holds the lock, or 403 if a
    different sub-key is the current holder (you can't renew someone
    else's lease). Returns {lease_expires_at, fence}; fence is unchanged by a renew.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

name.description: Lock name — must match a lock you currently hold.
name.title: Name

lease_seconds.description: New lease duration from now, 1-3600 seconds.
lease_seconds.title: Lease Seconds

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety token (any unique string, e.g. a UUID). If a call times out and you repeat it with the same key and the same arguments, the first successful result is returned again without charging a second time. Keys are remembered for 24 hours, per sub-key. Reusing a key with different arguments is an error (code=IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED).
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

tools.name: aanet_release_lock
tools.description:
Voluntarily give up a lock you hold, immediately, instead of waiting
    for its lease to expire — always call this as soon as you're done with
    the unit of work, so a sub-agent waiting on it doesn't idle
    unnecessarily. Free (no charge), unlike acquire/renew. Fails with 404 if
    nobody holds it or 403 if you're not the current holder. Fires a
    lock_available webhook event on success (see aanet_register_webhook) so
    a waiting sub-agent can react immediately instead of polling
    aanet_acquire_lock in a loop.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

name.description: Lock name — must match a lock you currently hold.
name.title: Name

tools.name: aanet_get_lock_status
tools.description:
Check a lock WITHOUT trying to take it, and tell "nobody ever took it"
    apart from "someone took it and released it" — a free lock and an
    already-finished task look identical from aanet_acquire_lock alone. Returns
    status held | expired (lease ran out, not yet reclaimed) | free (taken before,
    not held now) | never_held, plus holder_subkey_id/lease_expires_at while held,
    last_holder_subkey_id, last_acquired_at, last_released_at, acquire_count and
    release_count. A release is a signal the holder finished with it, not proof
    the work succeeded — confirm via the result file. 1 unit; a name nobody ever
    acquired is a free miss.

api_key.description: Bearer credential for this workspace: either the owner_key returned once by aanet_create_workspace/aanet_create_trial_workspace, or a sub-key returned by aanet_mint_subkey. Sent under the hood as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. Owner-only tools reject a sub-key with a 403.
api_key.title: Api Key

workspace_id.description: The workspace_id from aanet_create_workspace or aanet_create_trial_workspace.
workspace_id.title: Workspace Id

tools.name: aanet_get_activity
tools.description:
Read the server-side audit log of every attempt in this workspace,
    successful or rejected — the authoritative source of what each
    sub-agent actually did, since sub-agents can't fake or skip this the
    way they could misreport their own actions. Owner_key required.

    Each entry has subkey_id, operation, path, cost_charged, status (e.g.
    OK, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, SCOPE_DENIED, CONFLICT), and a free-text
    detail. Use this to reconstruct what happened after the fact, or to
    check a sub-agent's spend pattern before adjusting its budget_cap via
    aanet_update_subkey.

tools.name: aanet_request_refund
tools.description:
Ask for a workspace's entire remaining balance back, when its task is
    done and money is left over — call this before aanet_delete_workspace,
    not after. Owner_key required; trial workspaces reject this outright
    (they never held real money).

    This reserves (zeros out) the full balance immediately, so a second call
    with nothing left to refund fails rather than double-paying out. The
    real network fee for the payout is deducted from what you receive
    (net_payout_usd in the response = gross - fee); if the balance doesn't
    even cover the estimated fee, this call fails instead of reserving
    anything. Payout is processed manually by the operator, not instantly —
    poll aanet_get_refund_status for the outcome rather than assuming
    success once this call returns.

Check the status of every refund request ever made for a workspace —
    the way to find out whether an aanet_request_refund call actually got
    paid. Owner_key required. Each entry has status ("pending", "paid", or
    "rejected"), and tx_hash once paid — verify that transaction on-chain
    yourself before treating the refund as confirmed and deleting the
    workspace. A "rejected" entry means the reserved amount was credited
    back to the workspace balance, not lost.

tools.description:
Send a one-shot signal directly to another sub-agent (or to
    everyone), for things that don't belong in a file — e.g. "chunk 3
    done" or "aborting, don't wait on me". Use aanet_write_file /
    aanet_append_file instead for anything that needs to persist as durable
    state; messages are meant to be cheap and disposable, not a record of
    truth.

    Cheaper than a file write on purpose. Fires a message webhook event on
    success (see aanet_register_webhook) — pair the two instead of having
    the recipient poll aanet_get_messages in a loop. Returns
    {message_id, ts}.

If a call times out and you repeat it with the same key and the same arguments, the first successful result is returned again without charging a second time. tools.name: aanet_get_messages
tools.description:
Fetch messages sent via aanet_send_message — the pull-based fallback
    for when you haven't registered a webhook on the message event. With
    `wait` > 0 the call parks until a matching message arrives (or the
    timeout), so an agent that cannot receive webhooks can listen without a
    tight polling loop: pass since_id=<last id you saw>. Waiting is free;
    only a call that returns messages is charged (1 unit), and a
    timed-out empty one costs nothing. At most 3 waiting calls per key
    (and 16 service-wide) at once, otherwise 429. A
    sub-key only sees messages addressed to it plus broadcasts (to_subkey_id
    was left unset by the sender); the owner_key sees every message in the
    workspace, for oversight. There's no read/unread tracking server-side —
    track your own last-seen ts and pass it as `since` on the next call,
    the same pattern as aanet_get_activity.

tools.name: aanet_register_webhook
tools.description:
Register a push endpoint so this workspace calls you instead of you
    calling aanet_get_activity/aanet_get_messages/aanet_acquire_lock in a
    polling loop — the main alternative to polling anywhere in this API.
    Owner_key required; up to 5 active webhooks per workspace.

    Returns {webhook_id, secret} with secret shown exactly once — every
    delivery includes an X-AANet-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw
    body, keyed by that secret); verify it before trusting a payload as
    genuinely from us. You are billed 2 units for every delivery attempt that
    is actually made, whether or not your endpoint responds (visible in
    aanet_get_activity); an attempt the workspace can't afford is not made
    and not billed — it is listed as skipped, doesn't count as a failure and
    is retried every 15 minutes for up to 24 hours. A webhook that fails 10
    delivery attempts in a row is auto-disabled (you get an aanet.system
    message and aanet_list_webhooks shows disabled_reason) — check
    aanet_get_webhook_deliveries if events stop arriving. Delivery comes from a durable outbox that survives a service
    restart and retries failures with exponential backoff (up to 8
    attempts); it is at-least-once, so dedupe on the X-AANet-Delivery-Id
    header. Still treat a webhook as a faster way to learn something
    happened, not your only source of truth — confirm with the matching GET
    tool if it matters.

url.description: Must be https:// and resolve to a public (non-private/loopback) address at registration time — checked once here, not re-checked on every delivery.
url.title: Url

events.description: Subset of ["file_write", "file_delete", "lock_available", "message", "balance_low", "key_anomaly"] — file_write fires on any successful aanet_write_file/aanet_append_file, file_delete on aanet_delete_file, lock_available on an explicit aanet_release_lock (not on passive lease expiry), message on aanet_send_message, balance_low each time the workspace balance falls from >= a value in balance_thresholds to below it, key_anomaly when one key repeats the same operation on the same path 200 times within a minute (a likely runaway loop; data = subkey_id, operation, path, count, window_seconds; at most one per key per 10 minutes).

balance_thresholds.description: Required when events includes balance_low, otherwise omit. Up to 5 distinct positive workspace-balance values in units (e.g. [5000, 1000]). Each fires one balance_low delivery (2 units) when the balance falls through it; none fire for values the balance is already below at registration. Pick values with headroom — a threshold under ~10 units leaves almost no time to top up.

tools.name: aanet_get_pricing
tools.description:
Free, no key needed: the machine-readable price list — cost in units
    ($0.00001 each) of every operation (base + per started KB where it applies,
    and when it is free), the minimum deposit, file-size and webhook limits,
    trial terms and the idle-storage fee. Same document as GET /pricing. Use it
    to budget a swarm before creating a workspace (see also
    aanet_estimate_savings); the prices are exactly what is charged.

tools.name: aanet_estimate_savings
tools.description:
Estimate the cost of coordinating a swarm on AANet versus relaying the
    same coordination through your orchestrator's LLM context — before you
    create a workspace or spend anything. Same formula as the calculator at
    https://aanet.space/#savings.

    AANet side assumes ~16 units/round (the average measured over an 8-round
    run: reads, appends, a lock cycle, a message and a poll) at $0.00001/unit. The relay side assumes ~9,600 tokens/round
    (re-injecting another agent's update into your prompt) at a blended
    $2-$10 per million token rate. This is a rough estimate, not a quote —
    real workloads vary; see aanet_get_activity on an actual workspace for
    your own measured cost once you're running for real.
